BREAKING: Home prices across America's 20 largest cities rose +0.3% MoM in August, marking their 5th consecutive monthly increase.

YoY, prices jumped +2.7%, bringing the 20-City Composite Home Price Index to a record 346.6 points.

Since the start of 2019, home prices have surged +56.5%. 

Chicago led all metros in August for the 6th consecutive month, recording a +6.7% YoY increase.

New York and Cleveland followed, with YoY increases of +6.2% and +4.3%, respectively.

Housing affordability continues to deteriorate.

Demand is becoming a bigger driver of US inflation:

Demand-driven components contributed +1.2 percentage points to the +3.4% YoY increase in PCE inflation in August, the largest contribution since September 2023.

At the same time, supply-driven factors added +1.0 percentage point, while ambiguous factors accounted for another +1.2 percentage points.

This contrasts with the post-pandemic inflation surge, when supply disruptions were the main driver.

In 2022, supply-driven components contributed an average of +3.1 percentage points per month to headline PCE inflation, compared with +2.6 percentage points per month from demand-driven factors.

BREAKING: Fed Chair Warsh announces plans to overhaul the Fed's meeting schedule beginning in Fall 2027.

Under the new framework, one of the Fed's 8 annual meetings will focus on long-term strategy rather than voting on interest rates.

By 2028, Warsh expects just 6 interest rate-setting meetings per year, down from the current 8.

This will mark one of the biggest changes to the Fed's monetary policy process in decades.

BREAKING: The Consumer Confidence Index surged +7.5 points in October, to 91.7, its highest since May 2026.

This marks its largest monthly increase since May 2025.

The Present Situation Index jumped +8.6 points, to 120.4, its highest since April.

At the same time, the Expectations Index rose +6.9 points, to 72.6, nearly reversing 3 consecutive monthly declines.

The increase in sentiment was largely driven by the recent decline in retail gasoline prices, which provided some relief to household budgets.

Furthermore, consumers reported improved perceptions of the job market and business conditions.

Consumer confidence remains highly volatile.

It's officially Fed day.

We expect a "hawkish pause" today.

The Fed will hold interest rates unchanged but lay the groundwork for a December rate hike, bringing total rate hikes in 2026 to +50 basis points.

Why?

Because the US economy is now facing both supply-side and rising demand-side inflationary pressures, while the labor market continues to weaken beneath the surface.

This puts the Fed in an increasingly difficult position: Inflation is demanding tighter monetary policy, while underlying labor market weakness is calling for the opposite.

We expect the Fed to prioritize inflation today, keeping the door open for further tightening in December.

This result matters more for the Iran war than I first assumed. 

Exit polls show Netanyahu’s bloc falling from 68 to roughly 50 seats. Neither bloc reaches 61, and the Arab parties, at 17–18 seats, are effectively kingmakers. 

Netanyahu is likely on his way out, though nothing is final until a coalition is formed, and that process realistically takes six to ten weeks, with a repeat election a real possibility.

Until then, Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister with formal war powers. There’s no leadership vacuum, but his political room has collapsed.
